# Emergency Medicine
## Action order
1. Stop massive external bleeding. 2. Check oxygenation, circulating blood, perfusion, and cardiac rhythm. 3. Provide oxygen support or assisted ventilation. 4. Perform CPR when circulation is absent. 5. Use a defibrillator for a shockable rhythm. 6. Restore circulating volume. 7. Treat the source of trauma or systemic failure.
## CPR
- Item: empty hand. - Requirement: patient is lying down and has no circulation. - Use: click the patient with an empty hand. - Effect: temporary assisted perfusion and slower brain deterioration.
## Ventilation
- Item: [color=#58e6d9]NCManualVentilator[/color]. - Use: apply it to a patient with inadequate respiration. - Effect: temporary ventilation and oxygenation support.
## Crystalloid
- Item: [color=#58e6d9]NCCrystalloidBag[/color]. - Effect: increases effective circulating volume.
## Blood
- Item: a compatible [color=#58e6d9]Bloodpack[/color]. - Effect: adds blood to the bloodstream solution and restores oxygen-carrying volume.
## Defibrillation
- Item: [color=#58e6d9]Defibrillator[/color]. - Requirement: [color=#76e69a]Shockable arrest[/color] rhythm. - Effect: attempts to restore a normal rhythm. - Follow-up: recheck rhythm, oxygenation, and perfusion.
## Arrest states
- [color=#ffcc66]Clinical arrest[/color] — circulation has stopped while the brain can still remain viable. - [color=#ff5c5c]Brain dead[/color] — irreversible loss of brain function.
